headline: Revenue and margins surge, losses nearly disappear
summary_short: Caris Life Sciences' Q1 2026 revenue rose 79% y/y to $216.2 million on strong molecular profiling demand, with gross margin up roughly 1,800bps to 65% and net loss narrowing to $0.5 million from $102.6 million a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue grew 79% y/y to $216.2M, driven by 85% growth in molecular profiling services on higher clinical case volume and ASP gains; gross margin expanded to 65% from 47% as cost of services grew only 17% versus 79% revenue growth. Operating expenses rose 18% on higher stock-based compensation and headcount. Net loss narrowed to $0.5M from $102.6M, helped by the absence of FY2025 Q1's $32.3M fair-value charge and $24.5M preferred-stock accretion. Operating cash flow was $32.9M (+205% y/y) on improved reimbursement; free cash flow was $22.5M after $10.3M capex. Cash was $819.9M; long-term debt $381.1M, refinanced April 1 into a new $400M term loan. FY2026 revenue guidance of $1.0-1.02B was reaffirmed.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by 85% growth in molecular profiling services revenue, from higher clinical case volume and ASP improvements across therapy selection solutions.
Margin expansion is arithmetic: cost of services grew only about 17% while revenue grew 79%, so gross profit outpaced cost growth.
Operating expenses rose 18% on higher stock-based compensation expense and headcount-related costs, growing far slower than revenue's 79% gain.
Net loss narrowed mainly because FY2025 Q1 included a $32.3M non-cash fair-value loss on financial instruments and a $24.5M preferred-stock accretion charge, both absent this quarter post-IPO.
Loss per share fell to $0.00 as the much smaller net loss was spread over roughly 7.9x more weighted-average shares following 2025 IPO issuance.
Same drivers as basic EPS: a far smaller net loss divided across a much larger post-IPO diluted share count.
The improvement was driven by improved reimbursement from molecular profiling services.
Cash build reflects $32.9M operating cash flow less $10.3M capex, consistent with the release's own $22.5M free-cash-flow reconciliation.

The release discloses the company refinanced this $400M credit facility (effective April 1, 2026) at a lower borrowing cost with Blue Owl and Blackstone, though this postdates the March 31 balance-sheet figure shown here.
CEO David Halbert cited record February-March performance following a January sales realignment and encouraging Achieve 1 data for the Caris Detect platform ahead of its upcoming launch.
